nso.name: Statistics Korea (KOSTAT), now under the Ministry of Data and Statistics (국가데이터처); data portal KOSIS

latest_census.notes: The 2025 Population and Housing Census (centennial; field period 22 Oct - 18 Nov 2025 per Buddhist/Won-Buddhist press snippets) includes 'Religion', which 'is surveyed on a 10-year cycle'. Korean news snippet: results including religion 'will be announced in November 2026' -- so nothing from 2025 is published yet as of 2026-09-10. Ethnicity: the packet already declares 'South Korea's census does not collect ethnicity'; nothing in the searches contradicts it (the census counts foreigners by nationality, which is citizenship, not ethnicity). Language: no search result mentioned a language question; unestablished. The latest census WITH published religion results is 2015 (see earlier_census).

earlier_census.notes: Religion was on the 2015 20% sample form ('표본 집계 결과' = sample tabulation results, reference date 1 Nov 2015). National: 56.1% no religion, 19.7% Protestant, 15.5% Buddhist, 7.9% Catholic (Wikipedia 'Religion in South Korea' snippet; KOSTAT release: religious population 43.9%). Regional figures were published: a Catholic News analysis of the 2015 religion tabulation cites Ulsan 29.8%, South Gyeongsang 29.4%, Busan 28.5% Buddhist and North Jeolla 26.9%, Seoul 24.2% Protestant -- i.e. by province/metropolitan city (17 = admin1). By si/gun/gu (admin2): not confirmed by any snippet; the KOSIS search intended to find the table was refused (session search budget exhausted).

already_in_map: Nothing at admin1 (17) or admin2 (228); ethnicity declared not_collected nationally.

tier_reason: A census count of religion exists at province level (2015, 17 = admin1), but the only machine-readable form surfaced is an XLS attached to a Korean press release whose regional content is inferred rather than seen, and the systematic route (KOSIS) is a table-builder whose API needs a key; a si/gun/gu religion table was not confirmed. Ethnicity is not collected (keep the existing declaration); language unestablished. The 2025 census religion results land November 2026 and will supersede everything here.
recommended_action: Open the 2015 sample-tabulation press release (list_no=358170) and read its 통계표.xls for a religion-by-시도 sheet -- if present, that fills admin1 (17) from a count with no key needed. For admin2 (228 si/gun/gu), search KOSIS (Korean interface, 인구총조사 > 2015 > 표본 > 종교) for the 성별/연령별/종교별 인구 table by 시군구 and either download from the builder or register an Open API key. Schedule a re-check after November 2026 for the 2025 census religion release. Keep ethnicity as not_collected; add language as not_collected only after the questionnaire is checked.

summary: South Korea's census asks religion every ten years on the sample form; the 2015 results were published nationally and by province (a Catholic News analysis quotes Buddhist shares for Ulsan, South Gyeongsang and Busan and Protestant shares for North Jeolla and Seoul), and the KOSTAT press release carries a downloadable 통계표.xls. KOSIS holds the census tables behind a table builder and a keyed Open API, and probably tabulates religion down to si/gun/gu (the 228 admin2 units), but no snippet confirmed that table before the search budget ran out. Ethnicity is not collected, as the map already declares; language was not established. The 2025 centennial census asked religion again and its results are due November 2026, so anything built from 2015 has a known replacement date. Tier B: a count exists at admin1, but reaching it cleanly requires reading a Korean-language release or registering for a key.
